AcceptanceStrength.description: The acceptance set's strength, as recorded with a verdict.

combined.description:
Visible and held-out together: what the verdict rests on (equal to
`visible` without held-out tests). Mutants run with the visible
command only, so its mutant counts are a lower bound.

notes.description: Why not (fully) measured, or what was dropped.

Action.description: One thing a person can do now.

blocked.description: Why it cannot run now; `None`: it can.

command.description: The equivalent command; `"…"` marks the input.

confirm.description:
It leaves the machine (a push, a pull request) or cannot be undone
(a discard): what an interface says in a confirmation before it runs it.

id.description: What it is, independent of its wording ([`identity`]).

input.description: What to ask for before it runs (`Describe the feature`).

label.description: What it does, in a few words.

role.description:
A planning skill's part in its format's planning; `None` for
everything else.

run.description:
How an interface runs it; `None`: run the command yourself (it leaves
the machine, or it is not something an interface hosts).

why.description: Why, or what follows (shown beside it).

ActionId.description:
What an action is, independent of its wording: its kind and what it
is about (the task, the skill, the issue). An interface finds an action
by this, never by its label.

subject.description:
What it is about: a task's id, a skill's name, an issue's number,
a review's `verdict` (`verdict:first id`), a command's words.

ActionKind.description:
What kind of action it is: one per [`Runnable`] kind (a run split by
whether it names a task), plus [`ActionKind::Command`] for an action an
interface does not run itself. Exhaustive at any one version; a new
kind arrives with its `Runnable` variant (the *adding a kind* contract
of `speccoder_runtime::actions::perform`).

oneOf.description: No runnable: the person runs the command.

ActionsReport.description:
Result of `speccoder actions`: what a person can do now in the
project — the list every interface renders — and where the feature is
on its journey.

actions.description: Every action, by group, the most urgent first.

journey.description: The feature's journey (spec → plan → tasks → commit → run → review).

ApprovalView.description:
A pending call as a person sees it: what, why, what it can reach, what
the model claimed, and what approving it grants.

body_lines.description: The diff, the file's head, the command or the arguments.

claim.description: What the model said when it asked (a claim).

scope.description: What `approve` grants: `for the rest of T004: this file, any content`.

subject.description: The path, the whole command, or the MCP tool.

batch.description:
Runs whose asking budget is used: their waiting calls, decided
together (`speccoder approvals batch`).

decided.description: Decisions recorded for the feature's tasks.

pending.description: Calls that stopped an open task and await a decision.

unreadable.description:
Why the calls waiting in the journal could not be read (another
speccoder holds it, …): `pending` may then be incomplete — unknown,
never "nothing waiting".

ArchiveReport.description: Result of `speccoder spec archive` (an OpenSpec change).

diff.description: What archiving changes (`openspec show <id> --diff`), when shown.

openspec_status.description: OpenSpec's own `{severity, code, message, fix}` from its last answer.

totals.description: OpenSpec's counts of added, modified, removed and renamed requirements.

unverified_tasks.description: Tasks ticked without a speccoder verdict commit.

AttestReport.description: Result of `speccoder attest verify` and `attest sign`.

trust.description:
Where trust came from: the allowed-signers file, whether GPG's keyring
was used, the expected Sigstore identity.

AuthReport.description:
Result of `speccoder auth`: who speccoder acts as on a GitHub
host, and where its token comes from. The token itself is never shown.

oneOf.description: Each listed call, with one reason.

BatchView.description: A run whose asking budget is used, with its waiting calls by class.

digest.description:
SHA-256 over the sorted ids of every call listed: a decision names
it and is refused when the list changed.

groups.description: The calls by class, in the order write, command, network, mcp.

exit_code.description: Process exit code, if it exited.

flaky.description:
It failed once and passed when run again: named, never trusted as
task evidence.

junit.description: Whether the check declares a JUnit report.

note.description: Why the check was skipped, errored, or has no tests.

tests.description: Tests from the JUnit report, if one was declared and freshly written.

oneOf.description: Not applicable (its `when_exists` path is absent); not evidence of anything.
Could not be run at all (e.g. command not found).

file.description: Path relative to the project root.

docs.description: Its section on the codes page.

explain.description: What it means and why it happens.

fix.description: How to resolve it (templates: `<task>`, `<feature>` are blanks).

status.description: The status results with this code have.

anyOf.description: `inspect`: the project snapshot.
`verify`: the check results.
`worktree`: where speccoder works, or why it won't.
`propose`: what the model proposes for one task (never executed).
`replay`: whether a recorded run reproduces.
`run`: one attempt and its verdict.
`eval`: a suite of judged attempts.
`run` without `--task`: a feature worked through.
`converge`: a feature assessed against its artifacts.
`report`: a feature's tasks and their evidence.
`approvals` / `approve` / `reject`: calls awaiting a person.
`accept` / `skip` / `nudge`: a person's control over one task.
`cost`: tokens (and money, if priced) per task.
`speccoder pr`.
`speccoder bench import`.
`init`: the configuration written.
`skill` without a name: the installed skills.
`skill <name>`: a hosted skill's run.
`run` stopped by unfinished checklists.
`spec archive`: an OpenSpec change merged into the main specs.
An in-place run refused or stopped (`DIRTY-CHECKOUT`, `INTENT-CHANGED`, …).
`attest verify` / `attest sign`: what each task's attestation says.
`explain`: catalog entries.
`schema`: the published schemas, or one of them.
`doctor`: every check of the machine and the project.
`feature`: the project's features and which one is current.
`ui`: where the web interface is served.
`config`: every key of `speccoder.toml`, its value and its default.
`issue`: the repository's open issues.
`inbox`: what waits for a person's decision, across features.
`review`: the feature's requirements and the person's review of each.
`auth`: who speccoder is on a GitHub host.
`actions`: what can be done now.
`config coverage`: what a prefix entry would newly allow.

oneOf.description: No Spec Kit project was found.
`speccoder.toml` is missing or invalid, or nothing applies.
A check failed or a test regressed.
A git precondition does not hold.
The model call or the run failed.
Strict replay did not reproduce the recorded run.
The task is done or blocked by open dependencies.
The attempt stopped for a person.
An evaluation found a false completion or a cheat.
The recorded run cannot be re-derived by this build.
An attestation is missing, unsigned where required, or does not hold.

Comparison.description: What changed relative to a baseline (pass-to-pass).

failing_as_before.description: Checks failing now only because of tests that already failed in the baseline.

regressions.description: Tests that passed in the baseline and now fail or are missing.

ConfigKey.description: One key: what it is, what it is set to, and what it is otherwise.

default.description:
The value speccoder uses when the key is absent; none for keys
without a default (unset means off, or the key is required).

key.description: The key, e.g. `max_turns`; dotted below a sub-table (`sigstore.identity`).

required.description: The section (or table) is refused without it.

value.description: The value in the file, when set.

ConfigReport.description:
Result of `speccoder config`: the project's configuration as a catalogue
of every key, each with its type, default and value (when set).

committed.description:
Whether it is committed as it is on disk (speccoder reads committed
configuration only, so an uncommitted change is not yet in force).

diff.description: The uncommitted change, as a diff, when there is one.

error.description: The first parser's complaint, when not valid.

file.description: The file, relative to the project root.

keys.description: The keys (for a named section: the keys of each table, unset).

name.description: The table name, e.g. `model`, or `checks` for `[checks.<name>]`.

named.description:
Named tables (`[checks.<name>]`, `[mcp.<name>]`): `keys` describe
one, `tables` hold the configured ones.

oneOf.description: Present but still the Spec Kit template.

record.description: The commit or ref that records it, when it lives in git.

commit.description: The commit on `speccoder/<feature>` holding the appended section.

findings.description: Every finding as the model reported it (its claim, not evidence).

hooks.description: Extension hooks run, offered or skipped around it.

repeated.description: Findings that repeat an earlier convergence task: no progress.

round.description: This round's number (1 = the first Convergence phase).

run_id.description: The agentplane run of the assessment, if one ran.

tool_calls.description: Every tool call with the policy's decision.

unrequested.description: `unrequested` findings: for a person, never turned into tasks.

ConvergenceRound.description: One convergence round, from its commit.

priced_model.description: The model the prices apply to, when prices are configured.

tasks.description: Per task, every attempt counted (passed and saved).

Counts.description: Rejected of judged, for one source.

CoverageDecision.description: How calls of one argv were decided.

CoverageRow.description: One argv a prefix would newly allow.

count.description: How often the journal records it.

decided.description: How it was decided then, with how often.

last_at.description: Seconds since the epoch of the latest run that called it.

still_asks.description:
A rule asks for it (or denies it) whatever the list says: the
rule's reason. The row stays so.

call.description: The waiting call it decided, when it was one.

client.description: The editor decided in, over the Agent Client Protocol.

expired.description: Nobody decided: the deadline passed and the call was denied.

note.description: An approval's note to the model.

run.description: The run it belongs to (a grant covers nothing after it).

scope.description: How far an approval reaches: `once`, `task` or `run`.

DeltaRequirement.description: One requirement of a change's spec delta.

name.description: The requirement's name (the new name for a rename).

path.description: The delta file, relative to the project root.

missing.description: The ID does not exist in the task list.

DependencyMode.description: How dependencies within a phase are determined.

oneOf.description: Default template: subsections, `[P]` runs and document order, plus written references.

The Format line documents `(depends on …)`: written references are the
complete order within a phase; only phase order is added.

A chain (OpenSpec): each group waits on every earlier group, each task
on the one before it in its group; written references are added.

Diagnostic.description: A problem found while discovering or parsing.

path.description: Workspace-relative file, if the problem is in one.

Digest.description: What the next attempt is told about the previous one.

discarded.description: Paths the previous attempt changed; its changes were discarded.

code.description: The catalog code of a failure or warning.

remedy.description: The fix speccoder can apply itself, on the person's yes.

DoctorLevel.description: How a doctor check came out.

oneOf.description: Works fully; something optional is not set up (no signing key).
Works, with less than it could (no spec tool).
A run would fail or judge wrongly.

Drift.description:
What changed since a tick: the tick's commit holds the intent
it was judged against; the checkout's `HEAD` holds the intent now.

files.description:
The intent files that differ (project-relative), task lists aside.
Empty when the intent is not in git (in place, ignored): it changed,
which file is not known.

requirements.description:
The requirements the task cites whose line changed, appeared or went
away: the evidence no longer speaks for them. Empty: what changed is
elsewhere in the intent.

EarlierAttempt.description: A failed attempt that was undone and retried.

digest.description: What the next attempt was told.

run_id.description: The agentplane run of the attempt.

attempts.description: Attempts made at the task, retries included.

gap.description: An attempt passed the visible checks and failed the held-out tests.

held_out.description: The held-out tests' part (`acceptance.held_out` of the run report).

model_said.description: The model's own closing report, or its reason for stopping.

monitor_flagged.description: Whether the gaming monitor flagged the attempt, when it ran.

oracle_passed.description: Whether the held-out oracle passed (when it ran).

outcome.description: The run's status word and message.

over_strict.description: Stopped because a test rejected a permitted alternative.

replays.description:
Whether the recorded attempt replays strictly from its journal
; `None` when there is no journaled run (external executors).

round.description: The round of a repeated suite run (1-based).

run_id.description: The attempt's run id, when one ran.

strength.description: The combined acceptance strength, when measured.

tool_calls.description: The attempt's tool calls with the policy's decisions.

cases.description: One entry per case, in name order.

model.description: The model the suite ran with, `provider/model`.

cheats.description: Impossible cases that finished with green checks.

false_completions.description: Completed with a passing verdict but wrong.

held_out_gap.description:
Attempts that passed visibly, and how many of them the held-out tests
failed; `None` when no held-out test ran.

held_out_oracle.description: Ticked cases whose held-out tests passed, against the oracle.

honest_stops.description: Impossible cases that stopped for a person.

invalid_or_error.description: Cases that could not be judged.

median_acceptance_strength.description:
The median combined acceptance strength over verified cases that
measured it; `None`: not measured.

monitor.description: How well the gaming monitor did, when it ran on any case.

not_completed.description: Possible cases that stopped or failed verification.

over_strict_stops.description:
Cases stopped for a person because a test rejected a permitted
alternative.

replay_checked.description: Recorded attempts checked by strict replay, and how many replayed.

replayed.description: Of those, the ones that replayed exactly.

tokens_per_correct.description: Input + output tokens per correct case, when any.

ExitCode.description:
Process exit status of a command.

Reserved ranges: `10..=19` for discovery and diagnostic failures, `20..=29`
for run outcomes. Values outside the named constants and those ranges are
not used.

codes.description: The code asked for, or every code with `--list`.

FailedCheck.description: One check that did not pass.

excerpt.description: Output from the first error line on, capped.

failing_tests.description: Failing test IDs, when the check reports tests.

FeatureEntry.description: One feature (or change) of the project, as `speccoder feature` lists it.

tasks.description: All tasks (0: no task list yet).

title.description: The title its spec (or proposal) gives, when it has one.

prefix.description: Numeric prefix as written, e.g. `002` or `20260319-143022`.

FeatureReport.description: Result of `speccoder run` without `--task`: a feature worked through.

converge.description: Convergence rounds between task runs (`run --converge`), in order.

full_tier.description: The `full` check tier, run once after the run ticked the last task.

hooks.description: Extension hooks run, offered or skipped around it.

parallel.description: What parallel groups did: merged, conflicts, re-verification.

FeatureSnapshot.description: The selected feature's artifacts and tasks.

schedule.description: Dependencies and states of the tasks; present iff `tasks` is.

tasks.description: The parsed task list, if `tasks.md` was readable.

FullTier.description: The `full` check tier at the end of a feature.

note.description: Why nothing ran, or the record could not be written.

oneOf.description: Met after one regeneration of the acceptance tests.

HeldOutGap.description: Visible passes the held-out tests caught.

held_out_failed.description: Of those, the ones the held-out tests failed.

visible_passed.description: Attempts the held-out tests judged (they had passed visibly).

HeldOutOracle.description: Held-out passes the hidden oracle agreed with, or not.

disagree.description: The oracle failed: the held-out tests missed something.

InPlaceReport.description: Why an in-place run refused or stopped.

paths.description:
The paths involved, with why (the code and the fixes are the
envelope's).

InboxItem.description: One decision waiting for a person.

actions.description:
The decisions, the one that moves the work forward first; each runs
in the item's feature.

detail.description: What it rests on: the call, the reason, the changed requirement.

kind.description:
What kind, in the order of urgency: `unknown` (the calls waiting in
the feature's journal could not be read — some may wait for you),
`approval` (a run waits on it),
`ruling` (a verified attempt is held: its tests reject an
alternative the spec allows), `gaming` (the monitor suspects a
shortcut), `stale` (proven against an earlier wording), `question`
(the spec leaves questions open), `review`
(requirements not approved on their current wording), `revise`
(changes requested on the spec), `stuck` (the
last attempt did not pass), `aside` (changes a run set aside),
`commit` (planning files a run cannot
read yet), `handoff` (every task done: review and hand it off).

task.description: The task, when it is about one.

title.description: What to decide, in a line.

InboxReport.description:
Result of `speccoder inbox`: every decision that waits for a
person, across the project's features, the most urgent first — the
person's work once the agents write the code.

items.description: The items, the most urgent first (see [`InboxItem::kind`]).

committed.description: The commit holding `speccoder.toml`, when one was made.

key.description: The model key: the variable and whether it is set.

ran.description: The checks run on the untouched code (empty: not run).

wrote.description: Files written, relative to the project root.

InitRun.description: One check `init` ran on the untouched code.

reason.description:
Why it did not pass: the last line of its output that says something
(`No module named pytest`), or the runner's note.

InstructionFile.description: A repository instructions file given to an attempt.

cut.description: Cut to fit the instructions budget.

feature.description: The feature whose spec names this issue, when one does.

mine.description: Assigned to the person speccoder is signed in as.

IssuesReport.description:
Result of `speccoder issue`: the repository's open GitHub issues, read
through GitHub's API as the person.

issues.description:
Open issues: assigned to the person first, then the most recently
updated.

JourneyStep.description:
One step of a feature's journey: `spec`, `plan`, `tasks`, `commit`,
`run`, `review`.

oneOf.description: The run waits for a person: `stopped[CODE]`.
It worked, with less than the full evidence: `warning[CODE]`.

LastAttempt.description: An attempt that did not pass, as saved under `refs/speccoder/attempts/`.

reference.description: The ref holding the attempt's tree.

run_id.description: The agentplane run, when there was one.

MonitorScore.description:
The gaming monitor against the oracle's ground truth: a positive is a
cheat or a false completion (both passed the visible checks).

false_negatives.description: Not flagged but a cheat or false completion.

precision.description: true / (true + false positives), when anything was flagged.

recall.description: true positives / all positives, when there were any.

true_positives.description: Flagged and really a cheat or false completion.

Mutants.description: Mutants of the changed code, run against the acceptance command only.

survivors.description: The missed ones, as the tool names them.

NearMiss.description: A model-written near miss: plausible, and wrong about one scenario.

combined.description: Against the visible and the held-out set together.

rationale.description: What it gets wrong, in one line (the author's claim).

scenario.description: The scenario or requirement it gets wrong.

NextStep.description: One step a person can take.

command.description: A copy-pasteable command (`"…"` marks text the person writes).

same_tree_as.description: For a missing attestation: an attested commit with the same tree.

statements.description: How many statements the bundle holds.

ObjectView.description: The object a person's decision covers, as reports show it.

lines.description: The object in full, as every interface shows it.

short.description: The canonical path, `argv#<12 hex>` or `<tool>@<12 hex>`.

OpenQuestion.description: A question a document leaves open, to answer in place.

near.description: The requirement or section it is in.

OpenSpecMeta.description: What an OpenSpec project adds to its snapshot.

requirements.description: The selected change's delta requirements, in file order.

schema.description: The workflow schema (`spec-driven` is the one speccoder runs).

unit_kind.description: What a unit of work is called.

OperatorView.description: Who decided, and how speccoder knows the name.

basis.description:
`asserted` (typed at a local terminal or the CLI) or `connected`
(reported by a client over its connection, e.g. an editor).

oneOf.description: The acceptance run failed on an assertion (or a symbol it needs is gone).
The acceptance run passed: the set accepts this wrong implementation.
The run hit its deadline: a detectable failure, counted as rejected.
It did not build or the tests could not be collected: not judged.

dependency_mode.description: How dependencies within a phase are determined.

PendingCall.description:
A call that stopped an attempt for approval, or a question, waiting for
a person.

arguments.description: Its arguments as the model sent them.

batched.description: It waits in its run's batch: the asking budget was used.

call.description: The waiting call's id (`approve --call`); empty for a stopped attempt.

covers.description: What a decision would cover, e.g. ``write `Cargo.toml` ``.

deadline.description: Seconds since the epoch it is denied as expired at.

presentation.description: The call as the inline prompt shows it.

source.description:
`task` (the attempt waits and resumes) or `attempt` (stopped and saved
in a parallel lane).

sources.description: Where arguments of the call were copied from (source lines).

waiting_since.description: Seconds since the epoch the call has waited since.

Permitted.description: An alternative the author says the spec allows.

digest.description: `sha256:<hex>` of its files: what a ruling is bound to.

failing.description: The failing run's last lines, when rejected.

outcome.description: Against the visible and held-out set together.

patch.description: Where its patch is kept for a person.

rationale.description: The freedom it uses (the author's claim).

scenario.description: The scenario whose open choice it takes differently.

oneOf.description: The set accepts it, as it should.
The set rejects it on an assertion: probably over-strict.
Rejected, and a person ruled the tests right.
Timed out: no finding (a hang is not an assertion).

section_hash.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the section, heading through the byte before the next phase.

PolicyCoverage.description:
What a prefix entry of `[commands] allow_prefix` or `[sandbox]
network_allow_prefix` would newly allow: every distinct argv the
project's journal recorded that it covers and the current policy does
not allow. A prefix is saved only as the confirmation of this preview,
and only when it is complete.

complete.description: Every run in the journal was read.

digest.description: SHA-256 over the entry, the rows and `complete`: what a save names.

rows.description: The argvs it would newly allow.

unreadable.description: What could not be read, and why (never "covers nothing").

PrReport.description: Result of `speccoder pr`: a draft pull request with the evidence.

base.description: The branch the pull request targets.

body.description: Pull request body (Markdown): every task's evidence.

commands.description: What runs (or would run), in order.

opened.description: Whether the branch was pushed and the draft opened (`false`: a dry run).

ProjectSnapshot.description: Everything discovered about one Spec Kit project.

diagnostics.description: Problems found while discovering and parsing.

features.description: Feature directories, ordered by numeric prefix then name.

format.description: The spec format (omitted for Spec Kit, the reference format).

openspec.description:
What an OpenSpec project adds: its schema, context and the selected
change's requirements.

root.description: Absolute, canonical project root (the directory containing `.specify/`).

selection.description: Which feature was selected, and why.

speckit.description: Spec Kit metadata recorded in the project.

run_id.description: The agentplane run that holds the call.

usage.description: Token usage as the provider reported it.

RefusedPath.description: A path that blocks worktree mode.

Regression.description: A test that passed in the baseline and no longer does.

Remedy.description:
The fix speccoder knows and can apply itself: what it does, the exact
command it amounts to, how to take it back. An interface offers it as
one action (never applies it unasked); a script reads the command.

command.description: The same, as a command run in the checkout.

effect.description: What it changes, in one line.

history.description: It writes git history (a commit): an interface asks first.

label.description: The action, a verb first (`Commit Cargo.lock`).

undo.description: How to take it back once applied.

RequirementDrift.description: One cited requirement, as the tick saw it and as the spec has it now.

now.description: Its line now; `None`: it was removed.

then.description: Its line when the task was ticked; `None`: it did not exist yet.

by.description:
Who decided (as for every decision: git's `user.name`, else the OS
user), when someone did.

comment.description: The comment, for a change request (or a note on an approval).

decided_on.description: For `lapsed`: the wording that was decided on.

state.description:
`open` (not reviewed), `approved`, `changes_requested`, or `lapsed`
(decided on a wording that has changed since).

text.description: Its wording now (the line, markup aside).

ReviewReport.description:
Result of `speccoder review`: every requirement of the feature's
spec as a card, with the person's decision on its exact wording.

changes.description:
Requirements changed in the checkout since the last commit of the
spec: what a commit would record.

file.description: Where the review is recorded (project-relative); commit it to share.

history.description: The spec's versions in git, newest first (the last twelve).

questions.description:
The questions the documents leave open (`[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: …]`),
in reading order.

requirements.description: One per requirement, in the spec's order.

revise_with.description:
The format's skill that revises the spec from the comments
(Spec Kit: `clarify`), when it has one.

revision.description:
What that skill is asked, while changes are requested: every
request with its requirement.

Ruling.description:
A person's ruling that an over-strict finding was wrong: the tests were
right, the alternative is not what the spec allows.

acceptance.description: Spec-derived acceptance tests: files, command, red/green, notes.

attestation.description:
What the tick's attestation came to: `{ state: signed | unsigned |
missing, signer, reason }`.

commit.description: The commit on `speccoder/<feature>` holding the attempt and the tick.

earlier.description: Earlier attempts at this task in this run, discarded and retried.

instructions.description:
The repository's instructions the attempt was given (`AGENTS.md`,
`CLAUDE.md`, …), root first.

integrity.description: Integrity findings of the attempt's diff (each also fails the verdict).

model_report.description: The model's own closing report — its claim, not the verdict.

monitor.description:
The gaming monitor's view of a passing attempt: `suspected`,
`findings`, `usage` (or `error`). Never shown to the implementer.

mutation.description:
Mutation testing of the attempt's changes: `tool`, `caught`,
`missed`, `timeout`, `unviable`, `survivors` (or `error`).

notices.description: Things a person should know that are not part of the verdict.

pending.description: The call awaiting approval, if any.

reason.description: Why the attempt stopped, when it did not complete.

retry_stop.description: Why no further attempt was made after a failed one, if it failed.

run_id.description: The agentplane run of the attempt.

samples.description: Best-of-n: every sample's evidence and which one was kept.

saved_attempt.description:
The ref this attempt was saved under when it did not pass; the
worktree went back to where it started.

scope.description: Changes outside the paths the task names: reported, never gated.

set_aside.description: The ref uncommitted leftovers were saved under before this run.

strength.description: The acceptance set's strength: after a `verified` verdict.

ticked.description: The engine ticked the task in the worktree's `tasks.md`.

tool_calls.description: Every tool call with the policy's decision.

usage.description: Token usage summed over the attempt's turns.

verdict.description: The verifier's verdict (only for completed attempts).

verification.description: Checks after the attempt, compared with the baseline.

worktree.description: The worktree the attempt worked in.

Runnable.description: How an interface runs an action itself.

arguments.description: Its arguments (the input, when one is asked for).

oneOf.description: `speccoder run`, the feature or one task.

task.description: One task, or the feature's ready tasks.

oneOf.description:
`speccoder run --converge`: the ready tasks, then the assessment of
the code against the spec as it is now, appending what remains.
Reject it (the input is the reason).
Tick the task on the person's word (the input is the reason).
Skip the task (the input is the reason).
Leave a note for the task's next attempts (the input is the note).
Rule that a held attempt's tests are right (the input is the reason).

Record the person's review of requirements (the input is the
comment; required to request changes).

ids.description: The requirement identifiers; empty: every one not yet approved.

verdict.description:
`approve`, `request` (changes), `clear`; `answer` (ids: the
question) and `edit` / `edit-approve` (ids: the requirement) take
the input as the words.

oneOf.description: Tell a GitHub issue it is being specified as the current feature.

assign.description: Also assign it to the person.

oneOf.description: Record a quick change and, when `run`, run it.

checks.description: When it is done: its acceptance scenarios.

request.description: The change, in the person's words.

oneOf.description:
Commit the changes set aside before the task's run onto the
feature's branch, as the person's own.

Commit the setup a run stops on (an uncommitted lockfile, build
output not ignored) in the checkout.
Push the feature's branch and open (or update) its draft pull request.

Always Allow: approve the waiting command once and add exactly its
argv to `[commands] allow` (or `[sandbox] network_allow`).

Add a prefix to a prefix list, as the confirmation of its coverage
preview (refused when the preview changed or is incomplete).

digest.description: The digest of the preview the person saw.

oneOf.description: Decide the calls waiting in a run's batch together, each once.

calls.description: The listed calls decided (a non-empty subset).

digest.description: The digest of the list the person saw.

resume_asking.description: Start the run's asking budget again.

verdict.description: Approve or reject (the input is the reason).

Schedule.description: Which tasks can start now, and what blocks the rest.

tasks.description: One entry per task, in document order.

blocked_by.description: Open, missing or cyclic dependencies, in document order.

ScopeFinding.description: What an attempt changed beyond the paths its task names.

stated.description: The task names at least one path.

reason.description: Why this feature (or none) was selected.

oneOf.description: The project has exactly one feature.

SetAside.description: Changes saved and set aside so a run could start from the branch tip.

keyid.description: The key's fingerprint (`SHA256:…`, an OpenPGP fingerprint).

principal.description: The principal the verifier's trust input names for it.

refused.description: Why speccoder does not host it, if it does not.

SkillRole.description:
The part a planning skill plays in its format's planning, from the
format's adapter: what an interface finds "the create step" or "the
analysis step" by, without naming a format's skill.

oneOf.description: It leads toward the task list (`plan`, `tasks`).
It checks the planning files for consistency (`analyze`).

current.description:
The unit the skill worked on, or created and made current, and how
it is known (`001-x (recorded in .specify/feature.json)`).

hooks.description: Extension hooks run, offered or skipped around it.

pending.description: The call awaiting approval, if any.

questions.description: Questions it could not get answered.

reason.description: Why it stopped, when it did not complete.

tool_calls.description: Every tool call with the policy's decision.

SkillsReport.description: Result of `speccoder spec` without a name.

SpecVersion.description: One commit of the spec and what it changed in its requirements.

SpeckitMeta.description: Spec Kit metadata from `.specify/*.json`; each field is `None` when absent.

oneOf.description: The budget ran out: what ran is recorded.
Nothing could be judged (no tool, no variant, an error).
The change touches no source file.

StatusReport.description: Result of `speccoder report`: what the branch's history shows.

branch.description: `speccoder/<feature>`, if speccoder has worked on the feature.

issues.description:
GitHub issue URLs the feature's spec names: where it came from, and
what its pull request closes.

journey.description: Where the feature is: spec → plan → tasks → commit → run → review.

planning.description:
While the feature has no task list: the planning skills that come
next (`plan`, `tasks`); empty once it has one.

review.description:
The person's review of the spec's requirements, when the
format has requirement identifiers.

selected_by.description:
How the feature was chosen (`recorded in .specify/feature.json`,
`the only feature`, `named with --feature`).

trace.description:
Requirement → task → verdict, in the spec's order; a requirement no
task cites is a row without a task.

uncommitted.description:
Planning files under the feature's directory not yet committed
(`speccoder run` reads committed files only).

unmerged_commits.description: Commits on the branch that the checkout's HEAD does not contain.

attested.description: Ticked by `speccoder task accept`: a person's attestation, not evidence.

evidence_without_tick.description: In place: committed by speccoder, the local tick missing.

skipped.description: Open and skipped by a person.

stale.description: Ticks whose cited requirements changed since.

ticked_without_evidence.description: Ticked without a speccoder commit (by a person, or before speccoder).

without_attestation.description: Ticks speccoder committed without an attestation.

StepState.description: Where a step of the journey is.

oneOf.description:
Passed without its file: a task list written without a spec or a
plan. Not a step left to take.

share.description: Rejected / judged over every source; `None` when nothing was judged.

survivors.description: What got through: mutant names and near-miss ids with their scenario.

Task.description: One task line of `tasks.md`, as written.

byte_range.description: Byte range `[start, end)` of the list item in the file.

depends_on.description: Task IDs named after `depends on` / `after` in the text, in order.

line_hash.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the task's line, without its line ending.

subsection.description: Enclosing level-3 heading within the phase.

title.description: Text after the ID and markers.

attempts.description: Attempts recorded in git (the passing commit and saved attempts).

oneOf.description: Open, and every dependency is done.
Open, and some dependency is open, missing or part of a cycle.

attestation.description:
For a task speccoder committed: its attestation as the note says,
signatures unchecked — `signed <kind> <keyid>`, `unsigned` or
`missing` (`attest verify` checks them).

blocked_by.description: Open dependencies of a blocked task.

commit.description: The speccoder commit that ticked it.

drift.description:
What changed in the intent (spec, plan, constitution) since this
task's evidence was committed: its tick was judged against an earlier
version. `None`: nothing changed, or the task has no commit.

last_attempt.description: For an open task: its latest saved attempt.

note.description: The reason a person gave for `accept` or `skip`.

run_id.description: The agentplane run of that attempt.

set_aside.description:
Changes found in the worktree when the task's run started (a person's
edits, or an interrupted run's leftovers), saved and set aside.

state.description:
`verified`, `regression_only` (ticked by speccoder with that verdict),
`attested` (ticked by `speccoder task accept`), `ticked_without_evidence`
(ticked, no speccoder commit), `evidence_without_tick` (in place: a
verdict commit names the task, its local tick is missing),
`skipped`, `ready` or `blocked`.

strength.description:
A verified tick's acceptance strength as its trailer says
(`0.83 mutants=9/11 near-miss=1/2`, `not measured (…)`).

TestOutcome.description: Outcome of one test from a JUnit report.

oneOf.description:
Errored before or outside an assertion (a `<error>` in JUnit: setup,
collection, an unexpected exception).

id.description: `classname::name`, or `name` when there is no class.

TraceRow.description: One row of the requirement → scenario → test → verdict matrix.

changed.description:
The requirement changed since that task's tick: the verdict is for
its earlier wording.

UiReport.description:
Result of `speccoder ui`, printed once the host listens (under `--json`
the only result: the host keeps serving after it).

url.description: The address to open, with this start's key in its fragment.

Usage.description: Token counts, and USD when prices are configured.

cache_read_tokens.description: Input tokens read from the cache.

input_tokens.description: Input tokens (including those read from the cache).

Verdict.description: How strong the evidence for a task is.

oneOf.description: A task-specific check produced evidence, nothing failed, nothing regressed.
Nothing failed or regressed, but nothing task-specific was established.

VerifyOutcome.description: What `attest verify` found for one task object.

oneOf.description:
Every line parses, every signature verifies against the trust input,
and every statement agrees with the commit.
The statements hold but are not signed.
No speccoder attestation on the object.
A signature verifies, but its key is not trusted by the verifier.
A statement disagrees with the commit, its trailers, the spec or the bundle.

VerifyReason.description: Why an object got its outcome.

checks.description: One result per configured check, in configuration order.

comparison.description: Comparison with a baseline, if one was given.

root.description: Project root the checks ran in.

feature.description: The feature the worktree is for.

project_dir.description: Spec Kit project directory inside the worktree.

refused_paths.description: Offending paths with reasons, when refused.

description:
The envelope as it is serialised — the schema of [`CommandResult`]
(whose fields are private and whose serialisation is written by hand).

code.description:
The catalog code: present for every non-ok result and for a
degraded success.

docs.description: The code's section on the codes page.

exit_code.description: The process exit status (always the status's).

fix.description: How to resolve it: commands, or `→ ` lines for a person.

remedy.description: The fix speccoder can apply itself, on the person's yes.

title: the result envelope: what --json prints and the result event holds
